newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit trades in narrow range as volumes drop.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit trades in narrow range as volumes drop.

text.p: The ringgit was bound to a very tight range as trading volumes continued dropping in preparation for the year-end, dealers said on Tuesday.
"The whole market has slowed down. The volume has dropped tremendously," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said volumes in the last few days were just a fraction of average trading days as banks had begun unwinding for the year.
"We are not the only one that has already shut down for the year," he said.
Dealers said banks were still clearing some corporate dollar demand, but the small volume was unlikely to affect the market.
"Trading banks are positioning themselves for clearing their books, but are leaving some room for ringgit buying later," one foreign exchange dealer in Kuala Lumpur said.
Dealers have predicted that the dollar was expected to gain 100 to 150 points against the ringgit by the year-end.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5230/40 a dollar against 2.5237/40 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Monday. The Singapore dollar was at 0.5545/51 against 0.5446/49.
